title: OpenAI is sticking more ads in ChatGPT
summary: OpenAI is expanding its advertising presence in ChatGPT by introducing visual product ads in addition to text-based sponsored links. The new image-based ad format will initially appear when users generate images with ChatGPT, starting with US testing later this month. This expansion shows OpenAI's push to monetize ChatGPT beyond subscriptions, though ads remain limited to free users.
content:
OpenAI's latest ad format will put images of sponsored products and services on your screen. The ads, which OpenAI will begin testing in the US later this month, will "initially" appear when you generate images with ChatGPT, according to an announcement on Monday.
The company first brought ads to ChatGPT in February. Until now, ChatGPT's ads only showed a company's name, logo, and a link to its product in a "sponsored" section beneath your chat. OpenAI's visual ad format will similarly remain separate from the image you generate and will "not influence the answers ChatGPT provides." Ads won't appear if you subscribe to ChatGPT's Plus, Pro,  …
Read the full story at The Verge.

zh.title: OpenAI在ChatGPT中投放更多广告
zh.summary: OpenAI正在扩大ChatGPT中的广告存在，除了基于文本的赞助链接外，还推出了视觉产品广告。新的基于图像的广告格式将首先在用户使用ChatGPT生成图像时出现，本月晚些时候在美国开始测试。这种扩展显示了OpenAI在订阅之外的ChatGPT变现推动，尽管广告仍然仅限于免费用户。

title: TCL’s paperlike OLED phone made me more excited for the iPhone Duo
summary: TCL's P80 Ultra features a matte OLED display that provides a paperlike feel and low-power monochrome modes similar to E Ink screens. The matte display technology has been in development since 2021 across tablets and phones, offering a noticeably superior viewing experience compared to standard glossy screens. This signals how premium display features like matte finishes could become competitive differentiators in the smartphone market.
content:
TCL’s P80 Ultra is its first Nxtpaper phone with an OLED screen. | Photo: Dominic Preston / The Verge	

I've spent most of the last couple weeks using an otherwise unexceptional midrange Android phone with one amazing feature: a matte OLED display. That screen is by far the best thing about the TCL P80 Ultra, and weirdly, it's made me more excited for the iPhone Duo and its matte inner display.
2023's TCL Nxtpaper 40 first brought matte displays to the company's phones, after they appeared on tablets in 2021. Nxtpaper is more than a simple matte finish on a panel: it also includes a paperlike feel and low-power, monochrome modes that create a reasonable facsimile of an E Ink screen. But the matte effect has always been the biggest draw for me …
Read the full story at The Verge.

zh.title: TCL的类纸OLED手机让我对iPhone Duo更期待
zh.summary: TCL P80 Ultra配备了提供类纸质感和类似电子墨水屏低功耗单色模式的防眩光OLED屏幕。防眩光显示屏技术自2021年以来一直在平板电脑和手机中开发，与标准光泽屏幕相比提供了明显更优越的观看体验。这表明像防眩光饰面这样的高端显示屏功能如何可能成为智能手机市场中的竞争差异化因素。

title: Can Safeworld convince people that GenAI robots won’t hurt them?
summary: Safeworld is developing digital humans designed to address safety concerns about AI-powered robots and ensure they won't harm humans. The company's approach focuses on building AI systems that can demonstrate safe interaction with physical systems. Public trust in AI robotics remains critical for widespread adoption, making this safety-focused approach strategically important.
content: Safeworld is building digital humans to make sure robots don't hurt the real ones.

zh.title: Safeworld能否说服人们GenAI机器人不会伤害他们？
zh.summary: Safeworld正在开发旨在解决关于AI驱动机器人安全问题并确保它们不会伤害人类的数字人。该公司的方法侧重于构建能够演示与物理系统安全交互的AI系统。公众对AI机器人的信任对于广泛采用至关重要，使这种安全聚焦的方法具有战略意义。

title: Explaining Hall-effect, TMR, and other new types of "mechanical" switches
summary: Ars Technica examines emerging mechanical switch technologies including Hall-effect and TMR (Tunnel Magnetoresistance) sensing mechanisms that represent alternatives to traditional keyboard designs. These new technologies offer potential advantages in durability and functionality over conventional switches. Keyboard technology innovations can significantly impact typing experience and device reliability for professionals and enthusiasts.
content: Ars Technica's guide to new keyboard sensing technologies.

title: Google admits not every Android app runs great on Intel Googlebooks
summary: Google has acknowledged that while Intel-based Googlebook laptops support access to the entire Google Play Store library, some Android apps may not run smoothly on these models. The company previously emphasized broad app compatibility but now admits performance issues on Intel variants compared to Qualcomm-based models at launch. This reveals potential limitations in Google's cross-platform Android-to-Chrome OS integration.
content:
This Asus Googlebook is one of the Intel models that may have issues. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge	

Google has waited until the day its new Googlebook laptops hit the market to admit that Intel-based models may have issues running some Android apps. 
Before now, Google has emphasized that the Android-based Googlebooks give owners access to the "entire Play Store library" of apps, along with some clever interactions with Android phones and tablets. Today, in a statement to Android Authority, it admitted that while every app is available, some may not offer smooth performance on every Googlebook.

zh.title: 谷歌承认并非所有Android应用在英特尔Googlebooks上运行流畅
zh.summary: 谷歌承认，虽然基于英特尔的Googlebook笔记本电脑支持访问整个Google Play商店库，但某些Android应用在这些型号上可能无法顺利运行。该公司之前强调广泛的应用兼容性，但现在承认英特尔版本与推出时基于高通的型号相比存在性能问题。这揭示了谷歌的跨平台Android到Chrome OS集成中的潜在限制。

title: Our minds aren’t equipped to handle AI
summary: The article argues that human cognition is far more complex than the computer-based analogies used by AI industry leaders like Demis Hassabis and Elon Musk suggest. Industry figures often reduce human intelligence to biological computations, overlooking the deeper complexity of actual human thinking. Fundamental misunderstandings about human intelligence could lead to flawed AI development approaches and unrealistic expectations about AI capabilities.
content:
Norbert Wiener, godfather of cybernetics, once said, "The thought of every age is reflected in its technique." For the past century, our thought has been reflected in our computers, including by those in the AI industry. Google's Demis Hassabis calls the brain "a biological approximation to a Turing machine." Elon Musk puts it more bluntly, declaring that "people should just think of the brain as a biological computer." (Musk's brain often worries me.)
But humans are more complex than a straightforward comparison to computers gives us credit for - and far more than most of the AI industry seems to appreciate. And as their products push e …
Read the full story at The Verge.

zh.title: 我们的思想还未准备好应对人工智能
zh.summary: 该文章辩称，人类认知远比AI行业领袖如Demis Hassabis和埃隆·马斯克所建议的计算机类比更为复杂。行业人士经常将人类智能简化为生物计算，忽视了实际人类思维的更深层复杂性。对人类智能的根本误解可能导致有缺陷的人工智能开发方法和对人工智能能力的不切实际期望。

title: New forensic evidence supports Egyptian "retainer sacrifice"
summary: Fresh forensic analysis of First Dynasty mass burials reveals signs of fatal blunt force trauma on 39 percent of examined skulls, supporting historical theories about retainer sacrifice practices in ancient Egypt. The archaeological evidence suggests deliberate violence was used in what appear to be ritual burial contexts. This physical anthropological confirmation illuminates early state formation rituals and burial practices in ancient Egypt.
content: Fresh analysis of First Dynasty mass burials finds signs of fatal blunt force trauma on 39 percent of skulls

zh.title: 新法医证据支持埃及"殉葬"理论
zh.summary: 对第一王朝大规模埋葬的最新法医分析显示，在检查的头骨中39%有致命钝力创伤迹象，支持了关于古埃及随葬者献祭习俗的历史理论。考古证据表明在这些似乎是仪式埋葬的背景下使用了有意的暴力。这一体质人类学的确认阐明了古埃及早期国家形成的仪式和埋葬习俗。
